subject: Solstice annual renewal — request for executive authorization of one-time concession
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@solstice.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@solstice.ai>
Date: 2028-11-22T13:15:00Z
Subject: Renewal conversation — capacity, costs, and next steps

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the renewal notice. We reviewed usage and spend for the last 12 months (attached) and I need to be candid: our board is pushing for a 30% reduction in vendor costs across AI stack renewals this cycle. Solstice has been a great partner technically, but the math is tight.

Specific asks from our side: either a meaningful discount (they quoted 30%) or a one-time financial concession to keep economics stable for Q1. We also want tighter SLAs for uptime and credits for repeated incidents — those incidents drove most of the pushback.

We want to move quickly — can you share what flexibility you have and whether something can be approved internally within a week? I can loop our legal/procurement once we have a firm offer.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Infrastructure, Solstice Analytics
attachments: Solstice_Renewal_Usage_Report.csv
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@solstice.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-23T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — capacity, costs, and next steps

Hi Samira — thanks for the transparency and for sending the usage file. I understand the board pressure and timing.

High level from my side: we want to keep Solstice on Redwood — you are a strategic customer with growing footprint. I can propose a path quickly but it will require exec signoff because the ask is outside standard pricing.

Preliminary structure I can bring to leadership for approval (subject to signoff):
- One-time concession: 15% credit on first-year invoice (targeted to reduce short-term burden)
- Additional one-time operational credit: $25,000 credit to offset incident-driven costs
- SLA addendum: 99.9% uptime commitment for the next 12 months with a one-way credit ladder for breaches
- Condition: 18-month renewal term (to protect LTV) and quarterly QBRs for the next year

If that sounds like a reasonable starting point I will escalate to Deal Desk + VP sales for authorization and get a formal addendum drafted. Attaching a draft term addendum for transparency.

Can you confirm a firm internal deadline for an approval/PO?

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: Proposed_Term_Addendum.docx
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-24T16:45:00Z
Subject: REQ: Exec approval — Solstice (SOL-2028-0423) renewal concession ask

Team — escalating for authorization. Customer: Solstice Analytics (ARR: $420,000). Renewal scheduled 12/15/2028.

Summary of request: Solstice requested ~30% off renewal. Customer is sensitive to near-term budget; risk of churn if we cannot move. They cite multiple incident credits from this year as a driver.

My recommended package (what I'll ask to present to customer if approved):
- One-time invoice credit: 15% of first-year renewal invoice (~$63k)
- Additional $25,000 operational credit applied at renewal for incident remediation
- SLA addendum to 99.9% for next 12 months with defined credit ladder
- Condition: 18-month committed term; quarterly QBRs; a technical review session within 30 days

Why approve?
- Customer strategic (product integration, potential expansion into new lines)
- Risk of losing $420k ARR and >$1.6M pipeline influence in that vertical
- Concession preserves gross retention and keeps opportunity to expand next year

Impact: one-time revenue hit ~88k; % of ACV ~21%. This exceeds standard delegated concession (policy cap $50k) — request exec signoff.

Ask: approval for the package above or counter-offer guidance (preferred: up to 15% + $25k + SLA addendum). Legal (Laura) will need to approve the addendum language. Marissa, can you run P&L impact + alternative models? Vivek, request your signoff or direction.

Thanks,
Connor
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-25T09:30:00Z
Subject: RE: REQ: Exec approval — Solstice (SOL-2028-0423) renewal concession ask

Connor — thanks for the write-up, good context. I ran three concession models (attached Concession_Models.xlsx) — headline thoughts: 

1) Full one-time 15% + $25k (Connor rec): immediate churn mitigation but P&L hit is material (~21% of ACV).
2) Performance-linked split: 10% immediate credit now + $25k contingent credit payable if uptime and SLA targets are met over first 6 months. This reduces upfront hit and aligns incentives.
3) Term trade: offer 12% now + $25k credit + require 24-month commit instead of 18 — higher revenue protection but customer may push back on duration.

Legal note (Laura): any SLA addendum needs to explicitly narrow credit ladder and exclusion windows for scheduled maintenance. Also want to avoid open-ended operational credits — prefer defined credit amounts and conditions.

Recommendation: present option 2 to the customer (10% immediate + $25k contingent) and reserve the right to escalate to exec for the 15% upfront option only if customer refuses. If leadership prefers the firm upfront concession to speed the renewal, cap at 15% and require 18-months.

Attached: Concession_Models.xlsx with modeled revenue impact.

Marissa Cole
Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: Concession_Models.xlsx
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-26T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: REQ: Exec approval — Solstice (SOL-2028-0423) renewal concession ask

Team — I reviewed the models. Given the strategic nature and downstream expansion opportunity, I approve a middle-ground concession to close the renewal quickly. Approval details: 

- One-time invoice credit: 15% of the first-year renewal invoice (one-time, applied at renewal)
- Operational credit: $25,000 applied once at renewal
- SLA addendum: upgrade to 99.9% uptime for 12 months; credit ladder to be drafted by Legal (Laura) with clear exclusion clauses
- Customer commitment: final renewal must be for 18 months

Conditions: Legal must sign off the addendum; finance to confirm mechanics of credit application (how it shows on invoice). Marissa: proceed to finalize model and provide the number to finance. Connor: you have approval to offer this package and finalize wording with legal.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@solstice.ai>, Procurement <procurement@solstice.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-27T09:42:00Z
Subject: Final renewal offer and next steps (Solstice)

Hi Samira — thanks for the conversation and patience while I escalated internally. We have leadership approval to proceed with the following one-time concession package: 

1) Financials:
- One-time credit equal to 15% of the first-year renewal invoice (applied at renewal)
- Additional one-time operational credit of $25,000 applied at renewal

2) Service:
- SLA addendum to 99.9% uptime for 12 months; legal will provide the exact credit ladder language and exclusions

3) Commitment:
- In exchange, Redwood requests an 18-month renewal term and quarterly QBRs for the next 12 months

Next steps: I will have Legal send a short addendum (Proposed_Term_Addendum.docx) for your review. If procurement confirms PO timing, Finance will handle the credit application on the invoice. We are ready to finalize as soon as you confirm you can accept the 18-month term.

If you prefer the performance-split approach Marissa suggested (10% now + $25k contingent), flag that and I can present as an alternative — but leadership signed off on the 15%+25k option to move quickly.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: Proposed_Term_Addendum.docx
